title: IPAM fragmentation -> pod scheduling failures: incident review and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

On 2026-03-01 02:18 UTC we observed a multi-region pod scheduling failure impacting non-critical analytics batch jobs and several stateless sidecars. Symptoms: pods stayed in Pending with events '0/200 nodes are available: 180 node(s) had no available IPs; 20 node(s) had insufficient memory'. The root contributor was IP address exhaustion / severe IP block fragmentation in the Calico IPAM pool combined with a delayed calico-node reconciliation loop after a control-plane hiccup.

Why this matters: because our autoscaler and workload patterns assume available per-node IPs and rely on fast CNI reconciliation to recover when nodes are evicted or restarted. This incident caused ~1.5 hours of elevated pod création latency, 12% job backpressure, and increased retries across the analytics pipeline.

High-level timeline (all times UTC):
- 02:05: control plane flapping (etcd raft restart on 2 masters) causes transient API timeouts observed in apiserver logs.
- 02:08: calico-node pods in three AZs reported frequent FELIX sync errors; network policies still largely functional.
- 02:12: first pager alerts: scheduler reports "no available IPs" for multiple namespaces. Backfill autoscaler scaled nodes up but new nodes did not get allocated usable IPs quickly.
- 02:18: majority of pending pods show events indicating IPAM allocation failures.
- 02:45: we applied emergency mitigation (expanded cluster-wide IP pool / created temporary IPPool).
- 03:30: IP fragmentation defrag and calico-node restart completed; scheduler resumed normal allocations.
- 04:00: incident declared resolved; follow-ups assigned.

Immediate indicators and data sources examined:
- kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | grep -i ipam
- calicoctl get ippool -o wide
- calicoctl get ipam-block --all-namespaces | grep Host | sort | uniq -c
- grafana dashboards: networking-overview (IP utilization), scheduling-errors over time, control-plane latencies
- logs from calico-node (felix) showing ip allocation errors like 'IPAM: no free addresses in block' and 'Error while assigning IP to workload endpoint'

Root causes (summary):
1) IP Pool fragmentation: recurring small allocations and frequent node churn had caused a large number of Calico IPAM blocks to be partially full (<20% free per block) across many nodes. The effective addressable capacity was significantly lower than the nominal pool size.
2) Control-plane instability: an etcd compaction + leader election spike at 02:05 caused API latency and longer calico-typha healthcheck timeouts; calico-node delayed reclaim / block consolidation.
3) Incomplete runbook for IPAM emergencies: SRE runbooks lacked a quick safe recipe to expand pools or trigger a fast defragmentation/reallocation when fragmentation, rather than absolute exhaustion, was the problem.
4) Autoscaler behavior: cluster autoscaler launched new nodes but our Calico IPPool configuration allowed per-node limits or lack of automatic IP block assignment for newly added nodes which delayed recovery.

Contributing factors (non-root but relevant):
- Some namespaces (analytics-spot, experiments) use hostPorts and static IP allocations increasing fragmentation.
- Calico version 3.21 had a known but low-priority IPAM consolidation bug (see linked GH issue) that made block reuse slower under churn.
- MTU and overlay fragmentation across AZs increased fragmentation of endpoint lifetimes (VXLAN rehome events).

Diagnostics run (raw commands we used):
- calicoctl get ipam-block -o wide | awk '{print $1,$3,$4,$5}' | head
- for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do echo $n; kubectl describe $n | egrep "IPs:|Allocatable"; done
- kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/calico-node -c calico-node --since=2h | egrep "IPAM|no free|assigning IP"
- jq .status.allocations <(calicoctl get node <$NODE> -o json)  # sanitized for logs

Emergency mitigations applied (timeline + commands):
1) Temporary IPPool expansion (02:45)
- Created an overlay IPPool with a /16 range that didn't overlap existing pools to give headroom: calicoctl apply -f tmp-ip-pool-expanded.yaml
- This allowed calico to allocate from a fresh, unfragmented space while we investigated fragmentation.
2) Force calico-node reconciliation (02:55)
- Rolled calico-node DaemonSet rolling restart in AZs showing the worst allocation errors: kubectl rollout restart ds/calico-node -n kube-system --field-selector spec.nodeSelector=... (targeted)
- Verified nodes re-registered blocks after restart.
3) Autoscaler tweak (03:05)
- Temporarily relaxed per-node label constraints to let new nodes accept more pods and bypass static-ip namespaces.
4) Defragmentation plan (03:15 - 03:30)
- Gradually migrated pods from the most fragmented nodes to new nodes using cordon+drain with re-create delay, then calicoctl released blocks and new allocations consolidated.

Why the mitigations worked: adding a fresh IPPool decoupled short-term capacity from fragmented blocks and gave the scheduler available IPs. Restarts triggered calico node to re-evaluate block ownership and release orphaned addresses.

Impact summary:
- Duration: ~1.5 hours until critical scheduling rate restored; full stabilization ~6 hours (metrics normalized).
- Customers: internal analytics jobs delayed; no customer-facing APIs impacted because those services use reserved capacity and static IP assignments.
- Estimates: ~12% job throughput reduction for 2 hours, ~4 incident pages escalated to SRE team.

Post-incident action items (owner and ETA):
- SRE-34: Update IPAM emergency runbook with a step-by-step safe IPPool expansion + rollback checklist (owner: Asha, ETA: 2026-03-08).
- SRE-35: Create a scheduled job to compute live IP block fragmentation metrics and alert when effective capacity falls below 70% (owner: Marco, ETA: 2026-03-15).
- SRE-36: Apply Calico upgrade plan to 3.24 that includes IPAM consolidation fixes; test in staging with churn harness (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-22).
- SRE-37: Autoscaler policy change to prefer node pool with free ip blocks; add label-driven IP pool pinning logic (owner: Liam, ETA: 2026-04-01).
- SRE-38: Reduce hostPort/static IP usage in analytics namespaces; work with platform/infra to move to sidecar patterns (owner: Analytics infra lead, ETA: 2026-04-15).

Runbook draft (quick steps for on-call):
1) Confirm symptom: kubectl get pods -A | grep Pending; kubectl describe pod <pending> -> look for 'no available IPs' or 'failed to allocate IP'.
2) Determine if absolute or fragmentation: calicoctl get ippool -o wide -> check pool exhaustion; calicoctl get ipam-block --all-namespaces and run fragmentation script (included below).
3) If fragmentation (many partially used blocks) and pool has free CIDR headroom -> create temporary IPPool from pre-approved reserved ranges:
   - calicoctl apply -f /runbooks/tmp-ip-pool-expanded.yaml
   - Verify: calicoctl get ippool and confirm allocations increase.
4) If pool fully exhausted -> identify leaking workloads (hostPort, static IP) and decide between emergency pool expansion vs. targeted pod eviction.
5) Trigger targeted calico-node restart in affected AZs if blocks are stuck: kubectl rollout restart ds/calico-node -n kube-system -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=<zone>
6) If nodes are newly created but not receiving blocks, verify typha connectivity and check typha logs.
7) Escalate to networking SRE and open ticket to track defragmentation progress.

Fragmentation detection helper (one-liner rough):
calicoctl get ipam-block --all-namespaces -o json | jq -r '.[] | "\(.spec.cidr) \(.metadata.labels.CalicoHost) \(.spec.allocations | length)"' | awk '{ if ($3>0 && $3<--BLOCKSIZE_THRESHOLD--) print }'
"Replace --BLOCKSIZE_THRESHOLD-- with node block size (e.g., 256)."

Follow-ups for engineering teams:
- Platform: add cluster quota metric that reports effective usable IPs (not just CIDR size) and expose to autoscaler.
- Networking: build a small calico-block-defrag tool (proposal in PR) to run during low-traffic windows and reclaim fragmented blocks safely.
- Product: identify any non-prod namespaces with high hostPort use and communicate migration plan.

Notes and TL;DR for execs:
We had a non-customer-facing capacity incident driven by Calico IPAM fragmentation plus a control-plane interruption that slowed recovery. Short-term mitigations were successful and low-risk (new IPPool + calico-node restarts). The primary engineering work is to detect fragmentation earlier, automate safe remediation, and upgrade Calico to a version that improves block reuse under churn.

Appendix: Observed important logs (redacted)
- felix: ERROR ipam: no free addresses in block 192.168.34.0/24 for host ip-10-12-7-22
- typha: WARN client reconnect: rpc timeout during health check
- kube-scheduler: Skipping pod create: 0/200 nodes available: 180 had no available IPs

Contact list for future incidents:
- Primary SRE on-call: rotation-sre@redwood.ai
- Networking lead (oncall): net-lead@redwood.ai
- Calico SME: priya.singh@redwood.ai

Draft runbook file added to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/58 (contains tmp-ip-pool-expanded.yaml and helper scripts).

Attachments (to be uploaded to Confluence): calico-block-usage.csv, scheduler-event-snapshot-20260301.csv, grafana-screenshots.zip

End of incident review - draft.
